script.base: Closing line is JAX +3, total 43.5, outdoors, so the book has a competitive road favorite: LAC implied 23.2, JAX 20.2, not a blowout and not a shootout. Base flow is LAC up by a score late, both teams still throwing, with LAC mixing Vidal's recent 20-carry pace (60/242 in weeks 8-10) and Herbert's scramble runs (19/140) while McConkey remains the pass driver (22 targets, 251 yards). JAX stays in it enough to keep Etienne involved (46/186) but, as a short dog, funnels throws to Washington (26 targets).
script.flip1: LAC leads by two scores early, leans on Vidal/Patterson and Herbert runs, and pass volume stalls. That caps McConkey and the other LAC receivers the way a clock-kill script does, while JAX abandons Etienne's carries and Washington/Hunter/Thomas/Brown targets spike.
script.flip2: JAX hangs a lead or the outdoor game turns into a defensive slog under 43.5. Then LAC throws to catch up (McConkey live, Vidal carries die) or both passing games stall together if wind/rain, which is not in the pack, shows up.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not inactives: JAX CB Jourdan Lewis Out (Neck) so LAC WRs, especially McConkey, face a backup corner with no replacement named. JAX TE Hunter Long Out (Hip) and TE Brenton Strange Out (Hip) remove the tight-end room; weeks 7/9/10 already showed Long 6 targets and Mundt 6, so the next men are Washington (26), Hunter (14), Thomas (12), Brown (12) and Etienne as a checkdown (12 targets, -22 air). JAX T Anton Harrison Out (Knee) should raise pressure and cut rush efficiency, which hurts Etienne/Tuten more than short catches. JAX WR Brian Thomas Jr. Questionable (Ankle): if limited, Washington/Hunter/Brown/Meyers absorb; if full, Washington's lead is less automatic. LAC WR Quentin Johnston Questionable (Shin): last4 recyds 40, 30, 53, 42, all under 62.5; if he sits or is limited, McConkey/Allen/Gadsden gain routes. LAC T Bobby Hart Questionable (Knee) is an OL risk for Vidal's efficiency. LAC S Elijah Molden and CB Tarheeb Still Questionable: if either sits, JAX downfield and perimeter throws (Washington, Thomas, Hunter) face a thinner secondary. LAC FB Scott Matlock Questionable is a minor run-game piece. No practice-trend or snap-limit detail beyond these tags.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack, so shell is unknown. Team location splits only: JAX YPA left 7.17 (135), middle 6.81 (75), right 6.74 (130) over 9 games, fairly even and slightly softer on the left. LAC YPA left 6.2 (100), middle 8.97 (63), right 5.22 (138) over 10 games, so the clear hole is the middle, not the outside corners.
matchup.pressure: JAX blitzes 34%. LAC EPA/db is 0.17 when blitzed vs 0.03 when not, so Herbert has been better against pressure and a JAX blitz does not, by itself, kill Chargers downfield yards. LAC blitzes only 24%. JAX EPA/db is 0.09 vs blitz and -0.08 vs none, so Lawrence has been better when pressured than when the rush is four-man. Harrison out is the pressure adder for JAX's own offense, not a charted rate.
matchup.bleeds: JAX bleeds explosives through the air: 31 passes of 20+ for 352 yards in 9 games, while the run defense is ordinary-to-solid (4.30 YPC, only 19 runs of 10+). LAC bleeds the run and the middle: 5.00 YPC allowed, 36 runs of 10+, and 8.97 YPA in the middle, with only 21 passes of 20+ for 330 yards.
matchup.overlap: LAC's primary option is McConkey (22 targets, 251 yards, 219 air in weeks 8-10) into the JAX explosive-pass leak plus Lewis out. That is the cleanest primary-target overlap. JAX's primary option is Washington (26 targets, 175 yards, 324 air) into a short-dog throw script, two TEs out, and a Chargers middle that allows 8.97 YPA; alignment is not charted, so the middle overlap is inferred from air-yard volume and the TE absences, not from a coverage map. Etienne into the 5.00 YPC run defense is a real bleed, but Harrison out and a 1-of-last-3 rush over (44, 84, 58 vs 58.5) keep it off the card.

form: Last4 listed oldest to newest; last3 matches the pack's L3 yard totals. McConkey recyds 67, 88, 56, 107 vs a 61.5 season-median stand-in (3 of 4 over; L3 88+56+107=251). Washington recyds 29, 52, 90, 33 vs 33.5 (2 of 4 over; L3 52+90+33=175) with a 90-yard spike and a most-recent 33. Vidal rush 20, 117, 30, 95 vs 62.5, role is real (60 carries) but JAX run D is not a bleed and Hampton is absent from weeks 8-10 rushers (60/21/19/2 for Vidal/Patterson/Herbert/Miller-Hines) while still not on the injury report. Etienne rush 27, 44, 84, 58 vs 58.5, most recent 58. Gadsden 164, 77, 68, 13, trending to 13. Allen 119, 44, 41, 19, trending down. Johnston 40, 30, 53, 42, all under 62.5, and questionable. Thomas 80, 90, 31, 55 vs 52.5 but ankle questionable. No similar-defense splits beyond the season defensive totals.

pro_edge.script_read: Moderate total, not a volume-over shootout and not a low-total run slog. Spread is 3, so the dog-throws-more lean is mild and the blowout/starter-snap flag is off. If LAC leads late the lead back's carries rise; if JAX trails, Washington/Hunter/Thomas targets rise and Etienne's rush line is the one that dies.
pro_edge.best_price: No two-sided price saved on any prop. No-vig N/A for laddmcconkey recyds 61.5, parkerwashington recyds 33.5, and every other listed market. No Pinnacle, Circa, or BetOnline anchor. No book to shop. Alt no-vig cannot be built.
pro_edge.lagging: No open-to-close spread/total path and no book prop prices, so no lagging-line flag can be marked. Stand-in lines are 2025 season-to-date medians, not live posts.
pro_edge.sleepers: OUT: JAX CB Jourdan Lewis (Neck), TE Hunter Long (Hip), T Anton Harrison (Knee), TE Brenton Strange (Hip). QUESTIONABLE: JAX WR Brian Thomas Jr. (Ankle); LAC T Bobby Hart (Knee), S Elijah Molden (Knee), WR Quentin Johnston (Shin), FB Scott Matlock (Chest), CB Tarheeb Still (Knee). Same-position teammate prices have not moved in any saved file because no prices were saved. Hand filter: Lewis out points at LAC WRs (McConkey first); Long+Strange out points at Washington, Hunter, Brown, Thomas, and Etienne receiving; Thomas questionable points at Washington if he is limited; Johnston questionable points at McConkey/Allen/Gadsden. Treat as unconfirmed sleepers, not priced edges.

edge_players.edge_sentence: McConkey is the Chargers' primary receiver and already beat 61.5 in three of his last four (67, 88, 56, 107), including 251 yards and 219 air yards in the same three games Vidal ran 60 times, and he now faces a Jaguars secondary without Jourdan Lewis that has allowed 31 passes of 20-plus yards.
edge_players.must_be_true: McConkey plays a full route share, Herbert stays as efficient vs the 34% JAX blitz as the 0.17 EPA/db says, Lewis stays out, and the game does not become a pure clock-kill before he sees the 7-target range he has been on.
edge_players.kills_it: LAC leads big early and the Vidal/Herbert run game (60 and 19 carries in the L3) crowds him out, JAX brackets him with safety help after Lewis's replacement, Johnston plays full and splits the explosives, or uncharted outdoor weather kills deep air. A void if he were inactive is not the issue; he is not on the injury report.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, no Pinnacle no-vig, and every prop price is a season-median stand-in, so step 8 cannot size a rung. McConkey's pack counts agree with the over (3 of 4, L3 83.7 yards). That raw 75% recent hit rate is discounted to model_p 0.57 because legs rated 70-80% have calibrated near 50%, and because the total is only 43.5. Washington's L3 rate agrees (175/3 vs 33.5) but the game log is split (29, 52, 90, 33), so the lean is flagged for the human rather than sized. Etienne rush over was considered against LAC's 5.00 YPC and 36 runs of 10+ and dropped as a lean the game log disagrees with (44, 84, 58 vs 58.5, plus Harrison Out). Vidal over was not taken: JAX allows 4.30 YPC and only 19 runs of 10+, and Hampton's missing weeks 8-10 carries are an unresolved role risk. No 70%+ model claim is being used.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. LAC led early, Vidal and Herbert ran the ball the way they did for 60 and 19 carries, Herbert finished under 200 passing yards, and McConkey was the one LAC receiver JAX took away once Lewis was out, finishing on the wrong side of 61.5 the way he did in the 56-yard game. Washington's 324 air yards were empty again: another 6.7 yards per target, Thomas played a full snap count on the ankle, Etienne took the checkdowns behind the line, and Washington landed on 29 or 33 like two of his last four. Unsaved outdoor weather or a late inactive we do not have yet would explain the rest. That counter is strong enough to keep Washington a lean and to flag McConkey for a human, not strong enough to erase McConkey's 3-of-4 and the Lewis absence.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a clock-kill stack and not a shootout. Legs that win together: McConkey over if LAC has to throw to a backup corner, Washington over if JAX stays within a score and throws to the target leader with the tight ends out. A LAC blowout helps Washington and hurts McConkey; a JAX lead can hit both. Do not add a total under, a Vidal rush over, or any TD. Two legs, one market each, no depth-receiver lottery. No bet placed.
